great.name: Modern Treatments
great.quote: (d) Advance Technology Methods: ... The Company will indemnify the Insured Person for the Hospitalization Expenses incurred for treatment taken through following advance technology methods: A. Uterine Artery Embolization and HIFU ... G. Robotic surgeries ... H. Stereotactic radio surgeries ... L. Stem cell therapy: Hematopoietic stem cells for bone marrow transplant for haematological conditions to be covered
great.reference: Section 3.1 Benefit 1: Hospitalization Expenses, clause (d) Advance Technology Methods
great.explanation: Advanced treatments including robotic surgeries and specific stem cell therapies are covered without sub-limits. This means you can access modern medical procedures without restrictive caps.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: Room Category : If the Insured Person is admitted ... (i) Room Category = Single Private Room with A.C.
good.reference: Section 3 Scope of Cover (Room Category clause under General Conditions/Benefit 1 context)
good.explanation: The policy provides a Single Private AC room as the default room category. This ensures a comfortable hospital stay without extra charges for room type.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: iii. First 30-Day waiting Period – Code – Excl03 ... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are excluded for the first 30 days except accidents, which are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period in health insurance policies.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: a. Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.reference: Section 4 Exclusions, 4.1 Standard Exclusions, (i) Pre-existing Disease - Code- Excl01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 36 months from policy start. This is an acceptable and common waiting period in the market.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: ii. Specific Waiting Period - Code- Excl 02 ... Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Certain listed illnesses and treatments are excluded for 24 months from policy start. This is a standard waiting period for specific diseases.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: (i) As Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses during a period of 30 days immediately prior to the date of the Insured Person's admission to the Hospital; and (ii) As Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses during a period of 60 days immediately following the date of the Insured Person's discharge from Hospital,
good.reference: Section 3.2 Benefit 2: Pre-Hospitalization & Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization expenses are covered for 30 days and post-hospitalization for 60 days. These durations meet the standard coverage periods in the industry.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: Any Claim paid except for Benefit 4 shall reduce the Sum Insured for the Policy Year and only the balance shall be available for all future Claims for that Policy Year.
bad.reference: Section 3 Scope of Cover (General Conditions) / Sum Insured reduction clause
bad.explanation: Claims reduce the available Sum Insured without any restore or recharge during the policy year. This limits your coverage after a claim and is less favorable than plans with restore benefits.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Section 4.2 Specific Exclusions, clause (i) + Annexure II
bad.explanation: Consumables and many non-medical hospital items listed in Annexure II are excluded from coverage. This means you must pay out-of-pocket for these common hospital expenses.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: 6.2.2. Special Condition 2 : Co-payment ... (a) The Policyholder shall bear 20% of the Final Claim Amount ... (b) The Co-payment shall be applicable to each and every Claim, for each Insured Person.
bad.reference: Section 6.2.2 Special Condition 2: Co-payment (applicable only if mentioned in Policy Schedule)
bad.explanation: If this co-payment condition applies, you must pay 20% of every claim amount. This reduces the effective coverage and increases your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Co-pay Applicability
bad.quote: Special Conditions shall be applicable only if the same is specifically mentioned in the Policy Schedule.
bad.explanation: The co-payment applies only if specified in your Policy Schedule. You need to check your schedule to confirm if co-pay is applicable to your coverage.

unclear.name: NCB
unclear.quote: 2.1.9. Cumulative Bonus shall mean any increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase in premium.
unclear.explanation: The policy defines Cumulative Bonus but does not specify if or how it is granted or reset after claims. Confirm details in your policy schedule.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless Facility is available only at Network Hospitals.
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available at network hospitals, but the number and locations of these hospitals are not stated. Check the insurer's website for network details.

unclear.name: Sum Insured Exhaustion
unclear.quote: The Company shall have no liability to make payment of a Claim under the Policy in respect of an Insured Person, once the Sum Insured for that Insured Person is exhausted.
unclear.explanation: The policy states no payment beyond exhausted Sum Insured unless additional benefits apply. Confirm if any restore or extra Sum Insured is provided in your policy schedule.
